definition: The SEEKING system is described in affective neuroscience as a central command system involved in generating motivated, goal-directed activity. In this packet, it is presented as being activated in a drive-specific way when a drive engages a specific brain area together with dopamine release.

reasons: The phrase “involved in generating motivated, goal-directed activity” is not supported by the packet; the packet says the SEEKING system is of “central importance” and refers to generating “SEEKING activities,” not goal-directed activity specifically.
The definition adds a general affective-neuroscience characterization that is broader than the packet’s wording and not fully supported by the supplied text.

The definition states that the SEEKING system is “a central command system involved in generating motivated, goal-directed activity,” but the packet only describes the SEEKING system as “of central importance” among Panksepp’s command systems and does not support the specific claims about “motivated, goal-directed activity.”

The definition’s remaining claim about “drive-specific” activation requiring both activation of a drive-specific brain area and dopamine release is supported by the packet (dual action and drive specificity), but the first sentence remains unsupported.
